articles.title: Apple iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max launched: Check India prices, availability and all other details
articles.summary: Tech News News: Apple has introduced its first-ever foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The foldable iPhone Duo featur.
articles.body: Apple has introduced its first-ever foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The foldable iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer display, while the iPhone 18 Pro models bring a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture and longer battery life. All three models run on the A20 Pro chip, while the iPhone Duo is eSIM-only.Apple has also announced India pricing, storage variants and availability for the new models. Here’s a detailed look at the prices, availability and key features of the newly launched iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max models.​Apple iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and Phone 18 Pro Max India price and availabilityThe iPhone Duo comes in Star White and Night Sky colours. It is available in four storage options.StorageIndia Price256GBRs 2,99,900512GBRs 3,24,9001TBRs 3,74,9002TBRs 4,49,900Pre-orders for iPhone Duo begin October 16, with availability starting October 23 in India and more than 70 countries and regions. The phone will become available in another 28 countries and regions from October 30. iPhone Duo comes with an eSIM-only design worldwide. Apple says more than 500 carriers support eSIM, including Airtel, Jio and Vi.​The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max come in black, silver, glacier and burgundy finishes. Both models are available in four storage options.Apple iPhone 18 Pro: India price and availabilityStorageIndia Price256GBRs 1,64,900512GBRs 1,89,9001TBRs 2,39,9002TBRs 3,14,900Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max: India price and availabilityStorageIndia Price256GBRs 1,79,900512GBRs 2,04,9001TBRs 2,54,9002TBRs 3,29,900Pre-orders for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max begin September 12, with availability starting September 18 in India and more than 65 countries and regions. The two models will become available in another 20 countries and regions from September 25.Both models come with iOS 27 and support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. eSIM-only models are available in select markets, while India is among the countries included in the initial launch.​Apple iPhone Duo: Key highlightsApple's iPhone Duo, the company's first foldable iPhone, opens to a 7.6-inch display, which is the largest ever on an iPhone. It folds down to a 5.4-inch outer Super Retina XDR screen that Apple says offers 90 per cent of the screen area of the iPhone 18 Pro. Both displays share the same aspect ratio for proportional scaling, support ProMotion, Always-On functionality and up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness, and the inner display uses a nano-texture, glare-reducing finish with an under-display FaceTime camera.​Design: The device is built from grade 5 titanium with a mirror-polished finish, Ceramic Shield on the back and the tougher Ceramic Shield 2 on the front, and carries an IP68 water/dust resistance rating. Its hinge has over 100 components, reinforced with support ribs and ceramic fibre inserts for added rigidity.​Cameras: iPhone Duo has a 48MP Fusion Main camera, a 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide (shared with the iPhone 18 Pro), and a Center Stage front camera. Fold-specific features include Smart Take, Duo Preview, Kid Cue and Duo FaceTime, plus 4K/120fps Dolby Vision video recording.​Software: It ships with iOS 27, redesigned for the foldable form factor with side-mounted controls, dual Home Screen pages, Split View multitasking, an upgraded StandBy mode, and a beta rollout of Siri AI, which can use personal context and on-screen content to answer questions or take actions.​Performance and battery: The phone runs on Apple’s 2nm A20 Pro chip (6-core CPU, 7-core GPU, dual 16-core Neural Engine) with a vapour chamber cooling system. Dual batteries can last up to 31 hours of video on the inner display, 44 hours on the outer display or 24 hours of mixed use, and it has fast wired and wireless charging.​Connectivity: It uses Apple's N1 chip (Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread) and the C2 modem for improved cellular performance, with Apple Pencil (USB-C) support planned later this year.​Apple iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max: Key highlightsDisplay: Both models feature Super Retina XDR displays with ProMotion, Always-On functionality and up to 3,000 nits of peak outdoor brightness. The Dynamic Island has been redesigned to take up less space while showing more information, including up to three Live Activities at once.Cameras: The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max feature a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, bringing manual aperture control to the iPhone for the first time. The six-blade system offers four aperture settings and can automatically adjust based on lighting and depth of field. These phones also get upgraded Photographic Styles, Pro controls for settings such as shutter speed and white balance, and a histogram for checking exposure. Apple Reference Image can create a reference version of a photo using signed sensor data to help determine whether an image has been edited. Video features include Cinematic effects after capture at up to 60fps, 4K Dolby Vision HDR time-lapse and an updated Audio Mix.Performance: Both models are powered by Apple's 2nm A20 Pro chip with a 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says the GPU is up to 40 per cent faster than the A19 Pro, while the Neural Engine delivers twice the AI processing power. The phones also use a redesigned vapour chamber with three times more surface area than the previous generation, enabling up to 40 per cent higher sustained performance, according to Apple.Battery: The iPhone 18 Pro offers up to 36 hours of video playback on eSIM-only models, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max offers up to 45 hours. The iPhone 18 Pro can charge up to 50 per cent in around 15 minutes and wirelessly charge up to 50 per cent in 30 minutes. Apple says five minutes of wired charging on the iPhone 18 Pro Max provides around seven hours of video playback, while the phone can offer up to 30 hours of usage on a full charge based on its new battery usage model.Software: Both phones ship with iOS 27 and support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Siri AI can use personal context from messages, emails and photos, understand onscreen content and help users find information or perform actions. iOS 27 also introduces iPhone Handoff, allowing users with supported carriers to switch between two iPhone models using the same phone number.Connectivity: The iPhone 18 Pro models feature Apple's N1 wireless chip with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread support. They also introduce the C2 cellular modem system, which Apple says provides faster uploads than C1X while consuming 15 per cent less energy.​Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: 10 biggest features of Apple's first foldable phone, iPhone Duo
articles.summary: Tech News News: Apple has launched iPhone Duo, its first foldable iPhone, bringing a new design to the iPhone lineup. The iPhone Duo opens to reveal a 7.6-inch inner .
articles.body: Apple has launched iPhone Duo, its first foldable iPhone, bringing a new design to the iPhone lineup. The iPhone Duo opens to reveal a 7.6-inch inner display and folds down to a 5.4-inch outer display for regular use. Apple says iPhone Duo is built with a titanium frame, a new hinge, dual batteries and the A20 Pro chip. The new smartphone also brings changes to the camera, iOS 27, multitasking and Apple Intelligence. Price of Apple iPhone Duo starts at Rs 2,99,900 for the 256GB model with pre-orders beginning on October 16. Apple iPhone Duo will go on sale starting October 23. In this article, we look at the 10 biggest iPhone Duo features announced by Apple.1. Apple iPhone Duo display: 7.6-inch foldable screenThe biggest change is the foldable screen. When opened, the iPhone Duo has a 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR display. Apple says the inner screen is 50 percent larger than the display on the iPhone 18 Pro Max. It has a nano-texture finish designed to reduce glare and reflections. The inner display also supports ProMotion, Always On and up to 3,000 nits of peak outdoor brightness.When folded, users get a 5.4-inch Super Retina XDR outer display. Apple says it provides 90 percent of the screen area of the iPhone 18 Pro.2. Apple iPhone Duo design: Titanium body and new hingeApple has used grade 5 titanium for the iPhone Duo enclosure. The phone also has a new hinge made from more than 100 components. The company says the hinge controls the opening and closing of the phone and supports the centre of the folding display.The inner screen uses a scratch-resistant coating, a nano-textured cover layer and high-strength glass. Apple has also used custom adhesives and a titanium plate below the folding display. Apple iPhone Duo has an IP68 rating, and is splash, water and dust resistant.3. Apple iPhone Duo processor: A20 Pro chip and performanceThe iPhone Duo is powered by Apple's A20 Pro chip, the same chip used in the iPhone 18 Pro models. Apple says the chip is built using 2nm process technology and has a six-core CPU and seven-core GPU. According to Apple, the CPU is up to 20 percent faster than the A19 Pro, while the GPU is up to 40 percent faster and more power efficient.The chip also has a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says provides twice the compute power for on-device AI models.4. Apple iPhone Duo battery: Dual-battery setup and chargingThe foldable iPhone uses one battery on each side of the device. Apple says its silicon and energy-management system allow the two batteries to work together as one. The company claims up to 31 hours of video playback when using the inner display and up to 44 hours when using the outer display.When both displays are used equally, Apple says the phone can provide up to 24 hours of usage per charge. The phone can charge up to 50 percent in about 20 minutes. Wireless charging can reach 50 percent in around 30 minutes using a MagSafe or Qi2 charger.5. Apple iPhone Duo camera: 48MP Fusion camerasThe iPhone Duo comes with a 48MP Fusion Main camera. Apple says it can capture photos at up to 48MP and has an integrated optical-quality 2x Telephoto option. The main camera also has sensor-shift optical image stabilisation, a large sensor and a fast aperture for low-light photography.The phone also has a 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide camera that supports macro photography.6. Apple iPhone Duo camera features: Smart Take, Duo Preview and moreApple has added camera features that use the two displays. Smart Take uses on-device AI models to analyse a scene and automatically capture a photo when people are ready. With Duo Preview, people being photographed can see the live camera preview on the outer display. This can help them check their framing and pose.The phone also allows users to take selfies using the higher-resolution rear cameras while viewing the shot on the outer screen. Another feature called Duo FaceTime allows people around the phone to join a video call using the outer display. For children, Kid Cue can show Peanuts animations on the outer screen to get their attention while taking a photo.7. Apple iPhone Duo video: 4K 120fps Dolby Vision recordingThe iPhone Duo supports 4K video recording at 120fps in Dolby Vision using its 48MP Fusion Main camera. Apple says users can use this for slow-motion video. The phone also supports Cinematic effects after recording at up to 60fps. Its Audio Mix feature uses new algorithms to improve voices and separate music. Additinlly, time-lapse recording is also supported in 4K Dolby Vision HDR.8. Apple iPhone Duo software: iOS 27 and split-screen multitaskingApple has changed iOS 27 for the foldable display. When the phone is open, users can access two Home Screen pages and Today View. The system also moves some controls to the side to make more room for content. The iPhone Duo also supports Split View, allowing two apps to run side by side for the first time on an iPhone.Users can also open two windows from the same app, such as Safari, and save pairs of apps for later use. Apple says apps including Netflix, Zoom and Slack have already been adapted for the foldable design.9. Apple iPhone Duo AI features: Apple Intelligence and Siri AIThe iPhone Duo supports Apple Intelligence and the new Siri AI. Siri AI is rolling out in beta with iOS 27. Apple says it can use personal context from areas such as messages, emails and photos. The new Siri can also understand what is shown on the screen and take actions based on that information.Apple Intelligence also brings features such as improved Clean Up, Spatial Reframing, Extend and Image Playground. Apple says on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute are used for Apple Intelligence features.10. Apple iPhone Duo security: Touch ID in the side buttonThe iPhone Duo uses Touch ID in the side button for authentication. This means the foldable iPhone does not use Face ID for unlocking. Apple says users can also unlock the iPhone Duo using a supported Apple Watch.The phone has Camera Control, which can launch the camera and also supports a new Siri Camera mode. Apple says Siri Camera can use what the camera sees to answer questions and take actions.Apple iPhone Duo price in India: Starts at Rs 2,99,900The iPhone Duo starts at Rs 2,99,900 in India for 256GB storage. Apple will also offer 512GB, 1TB and 2TB storage options. The phone will be available in Star White and Night Sky.Apple will also sell an iPhone Duo Case for Rs 8,900 and an iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand for Rs 14,900.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: The Trump phone just got a $250 price hike
articles.summary: Even the Trumps can’t escape RAMageddon.﻿
articles.body: Bad news if you didn’t lock in a Trump phone at launch: It now costs $749, a $250 increase on its price at launch. The T1 Phone itself hasn’t changed. Trump Mobile didn’t announce the price increase, instead quietly changing its website overnight. This wasn’t a total surprise though, especially given the phone ships with an unexpectedly generous 512GB of storage and 12GB of RAM. When I spoke to two Trump Mobile executives earlier this year, they called the $499 launch pricing “introductory,” and a few months later, the website itself was changed to reflect that, calling it a “promotional price.” That wording is now gone. When I reviewed the Trump phone in July, I wasn’t especially impressed, even at $499. At $749 there is absolutely no reason recommend it. You could buy an iPhone 17E or Galaxy S26 FE and have $50 left over to buy a gold case; $50 more would net you an older flagship like the iPhone 16 or Pixel 10. Any one of these phones would blow the T1 Phone out of the water. To my surprise, my Trump phone has received some support since it launched. There’s been exactly one software update, moving it from Android’s February 2026 security patch to the May 2026 version. It’s still running Android 15 though, which is now two years old. While the Trump phone officially started shipping in May, almost a year after it was announced, it remains unclear just how many customers have received their phones. A report from the BBC last month found that at least some buyers still say their phones never arrived.

articles.title: The variable aperture isn’t the cool part of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera
articles.summary: Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and and Pro Max alongside its new iPhone Duo foldable phone. The new camera feature of the Pro phones is a variable aperture. But will it make a big difference?
articles.body: Apple always makes a big show of the latest cameras in its phones, and the major talking point of the iPhone 18 Pro is about the new variable aperture. Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have an adjustable mechanical iris in their main camera modules to let more or less light into the sensor, allowing users to shoot at f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4. You can, of course, let the camera select your aperture automatically, but the manual aperture control comes along with other new pro controls allowing you to dial in shutter speeds, manual white balance, and even manual focusing. As a whole, this is a wealth of new controls for an iPhone camera. You’d normally have to install a third-party camera app like Halide to do some of this, and now it’s all just baked into the 18 Pro’s native camera app. (It’s almost as if Apple poached a key person directly from Halide.) But I’d temper any expectations over the variable aperture being the standout feature. It’s going to be mid, at best. [Image: [Image: [Image: Why? Because smartphone sensors are still pretty dang tiny, and most subjects are in reasonable focus until you get really close. And stopping down to f/4 is unlikely to blow you away with much sharper results like it does in full-size cameras or any special qualities aside from some sunstar effects in very particular lighting scenarios. In fact, due to lens diffraction, your photos might be less sharp at f/4 than f/1.8 or f/2.8. What you’re most likely to benefit from by stopping down the lens is more depth of field with close-up subjects, getting more people in focus during big group shots with plenty of light (where people aren’t all lined up together), and more flexibility in shooting video in overly bright situations (like direct sunlight). That might prove useful for those particular situations, but they’re likely to be few and far between. And smartphone sensors are small enough to already have plenty in focus at midrange and further distances, even when shot wide open. It’s probably why other brands like Samsung and Xiaomi have experimented with variable apertures but quietly ditched them. I think the real star feature of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera is its f/1.48 maximum aperture. Fuck stopping down, man. People love bokeh. [Image: [Image: Last year’s Pro iPhone cameras had an f/1.7 aperture, and now being at f/1.48, the 18 Pro camera should work better in low-light as well as have a slightly shallower depth of field. Will f/1.48 be a huge difference in bokeh from f/1.7? Probably not. It’s likely to have depth of field that’s just a smidge shallower — but that’s the look that people often like. I speak from experience here, as I usually shoot on full-frame cameras and one of my go-to lenses is a 50mm with an f/1.2 maximum aperture. A lens that fast, with depth of field that shallow gives a unique look that’s easy to overuse, but it almost never fails that people swoon when I take their portrait using that lens — with that blurry, “dreamy” blur isolating them from the background. The f/1.48 of the iPhone 18 Pro is obviously not going to compare to an f/1.2 on full-frame, but f/1.2 and similarly wide apertures on big sensors is the look that people often want to emulate. It’s the whole reason Portrait Modes on smartphones came into being in the first place. The iPhone 18 Pro is likely to have a very good camera just like most top-flight smartphones have very good cameras. The added controls are exciting and fun, even if I don’t always want to be bothered with manual controls when taking quick snapshots. It’ll be nice to have them right at your fingertips without having to install a more specialized app. Just don’t be surprised if you start ignoring that aperture setting after some initial tinkering in the new phone honeymoon phase. But even long after that, f/1.48 will be the gift that should keep on giving.

articles.title: From school expulsion to free gurukul: A UP man’s journey of change on KBC
articles.summary: Uddeshya Sachan's journey from being expelled from school to establishing a free learning space for 400 underprivileged children highlights resilience and the spirit of social change, featured on KBC 18.
articles.body: Uddeshya Sachan, a KBC 18 contestant from Uttar Pradesh, shares on the show how childhood experiences of financial crisis and school expulsion shaped his decision to build a learning space that now educates around 400 students without charging fees. Recounting the severe financial crisis his family faced, which required him to work multiple jobs to fund his own education, Uddeshya opens up about the pivotal moment that changed his life's purpose by saying, "Sir, mere pitaji tailor the aur mummy ko ek baar current lag gaya tha toh bimaar thi. Ghar ki sthiti bahut kharab thi, rishtedaar thodi madad kar rahe the. Humare paas school ki fees dene ke liye paise nahi the, toh mujhe aur mere bhai ko nikal diya. Pitaji ki sthiti aisi nahi thi lekin unhone bahut sangharsh kiya, chaar hazaar ya paanch hazaar mein ghar chal raha tha. Dheere dheere kaise toh padhai poori hui. Ek moment mein aisa feel hua ki main akela nahi hoon, mere jaise aur bhi bachche honge. Maine joh mehsoos kiya, aur bhi bachchon ne mehsoos kiya hoga. Phir socha, maine idhar janam liya hai, toh jab main marunga mujhe kuch achha karke marna hain aur society mein kuch change lana hain."Deeply moved by Uddeshya’s grit, host Amitabh Bachchan praises his noble initiative and the immense satisfaction that comes from achieving such a meaningful goal by saying, "Uddeshyaji, main samajhta hoon aapne kaafi sangharsh kiya, lekin sangharsh karke jab aap jeevan mein uthte hain, aap bohot kuch seekhte hain. Ek aapka uddeshya hai ki humein jivan mein kahi toh pahunchna hain, aur usse poora karne ke baad joh santusti milti hain, uske liye aapko bahut bahut badhai."When asked how he manages the resources for 400 students, Uddeshya reveals that his mother initially supported him financially, and he slowly began sharing videos of his school on social media one of which was even amplified by actor R Madhavan. Hearing this, Mr. Amitabh Bachchan makes a heartwarming promise on national television to personally support Uddeshya's cause by saying, "Uddeshyaji, aapka joh social media hain aur usko joh sambhalte hain, unko bolna humein bhi bhejna. Aur humare paas bhi ek kuch log hain joh social media pe aate hain, toh unko hum bhej denge aur phir aapko patra likhenge ki humne aapka kaam kar diya hain."Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: Apple could make it a lot easier to redeem physical gift cards.
articles.summary:
The iOS 27 Release Candidate became available yesterday and includes new code that seems to indicate you’ll soon be able to redeem physical Apple gift cards by tapping them on the back of your iPhone, according to MacRumors. An added security chip, presumably NFC, will also help reduce scams by making it easier to tell if a card has been cancelled or already spent.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/giftcard.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

articles.title: This Qi2 ring charger has a built-in fan
articles.summary:
Charging your phone wirelessly can get mighty toasty. ESR’s new CryoBoost 25W charging pad has a clever solution: a fan built right into the charging puck. The company says the design allows it to charge an iPhone 17 Pro halfway up to 28 percent faster than the official Apple MagSafe 25W charger. Maybe I’m no fun, but once you’re plugging a cable in to run a fan while you charge your phone why not… just use wired charging? Anyway, it’s kinda cool, I guess.

articles.title: Snapchat makes it easier to plan events and meetups
articles.summary: Snapchat Plans formalizes event planing already being done inside group chat for birthdays, study sessions, and hangouts.
articles.body: Snapchat is launching Plans, a new suite of features designed to help turn the plans already being made in group chats — everything from birthday celebrations to study sessions and weekend hangouts — into real life get-togethers without ever leaving the app. Plans lets users set event details, invite up to 200 friends with invitations adorned with dynamic Bitmoji that change as friends respond, and track RSVPs. Invites are sent via one-to-one chat and reminders are automatically sent to attendees before the scheduled event starts. A dedicated “My Plans” tab on user profiles lets you keep track of upcoming and past plans. Snap is struggling to retain users in key markets, so features like Snapchat Plans, designed to keep users coming back to the app, could be critical to the company’s long-term prospects while its owner is distracted by eyewear.
